unknown: null means unknown or not computed; never 0

flags.what: while terrain_step_is_a_census is not true, word the terrain and cloud steps as 'among the areas with a terrain horizon so far' and read them from measured_cells_with_a_horizon; the first two steps come from all_measured_cells

meta.ai_note: computed by code written with AI assistance (Claude) from open data

lower_latitude_sites.what: flat horizon, standard refraction, Sun's apparent centre in (0, limit]; hours per 365-day year computed by twinfinder.sun at each site's own latitude (longitude does not enter); the profile_* values are read from latitude_profile.json between its two nearest half-degree rows, as a check

latitude_against_full_method.what: measured northern cells (gridded, bare ground at least 0.15, 59 to 84 N, snow status measured). A cell reaches a period with at least 100 long-window hours in it. Steps, each applied to the cells that passed the one before: sun_alone (flat horizon, long_flat), after_snow (times snow-free odds, long_snow_free), after_terrain (terrain horizon too, long_open), after_cloud (long_open times the clear-sky share of the bin's month, NASA POWER CERES cloud amount; mean cloud is not the chance that a low Sun is visible). unknown_cells passed the step before but have no value at this one (no horizon, partial snow odds) and are counted in no later step.

known_sites.what: each site is read on the cell that holds it. North: long_open_hours a year (2 h spells, snow-free odds, terrain). South: long_summer_rock_open_hours (27 November to 1 March, terrain; snow not measured). The percentile is the share of the ranked cells of the same hemisphere with fewer such hours (equal hours count half); high = top third, low = bottom third. percentile_flat_among_rankable is the same over a flat horizon among every cell that could be ranked without a horizon.
known_sites.ranked_rule: gridded, bare ground at least 0.25, a terrain horizon, and in the north measured snow (twinfinder.score.not_ranked_because on grazing_cells.json)
known_sites.caveat: With so few known lighting analogs this is a sanity check, not a test of the ranking: the sites were chosen for geology, landforms, life or logistics, never for Sun height.

snow_station_check.what: satellite snow-free odds against the share of days on which weather stations reported no snow on the ground, per station and ten-day period; with_stale_flag_rule is the odds the project uses

method.source: NOAA GHCN-Daily snow depth (SNWD), per-station CSV files
method.period: ten snow years, 1 October 2015 to 30 September 2025; a snow year is named by its October
method.bias: satellite (IMS, mean of the 3 x 3 pixels around the station) minus station; negative means the satellite layer shows more snow
method.n: station-bins: one station in one ten-day bin
method.stations: in a comparison: stations with at least one compared bin in that part of the year
method.trust_rule: snow depth on at least 80% of days (1 Oct to 31 Mar) in at least 5 winters, with zero depths and at least 10 non-zero depths in those winters; not bare on over 20% of at least 10 days that end a cold, wet week; reports that failed GHCN quality control are dropped; the station share uses the whole snow years (1 Oct to 30 Sep) of the well-reported winters; a ten-day bin is compared only if the station reported on 80% of the calendar days the bin holds in those snow years (15 or 16 a year for the last bin)
